not_covered: The EU AI Act entered into force in phases between 2024 and 2027 because the phased entry was deliberate, designed so that obligations would land as institutional capacity and technology mature [Source: ev-1].
This schedule also functions as a compliance roadmap for the "Brussels effect," which exports these standards to providers worldwide [Source: ev-1].

The different deadlines require specific actions based on risk tiers and system categories:
*   **Prohibited practices:** Practices classified as "unacceptable risk" (such as social scoring and certain manipulative uses) are banned outright starting from February 2, 2025 [Source: ev-1].
Violations of these prohibited practices carry fines reaching €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher [Source: ev-1].
These duties are scaled by systemic-risk status, specifically referencing a threshold of $10^{26}$ FLOPs [Source: ev-1].
A GPAI Code of Practice was drafted between 2024–2025 to serve as the safe-zone interpretation of these obligations [Source: ev-1].
Most other breaches carry fines of €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover [Source: ev-1].
*   **High-risk systems:** High-risk system obligations apply from August 2026, with a subset applying from August 2027 [Source: ev-1].
The Act itself entered into force on August 1, 2024, after being published in the EU Official Journal on July 12, 2024.
The European AI Office, established in Brussels in 2024, leads implementation [Source: ev-1].
